concepts.def: Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
Intracellular molecule (e.g. cAMP) that relays a signal from a hormone-receptor binding to enzymes inside the cell.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordination & Control — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordination & Control brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordination & Control.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Adrenaline binds to receptors on the membrane and activates:
options: DNA directly
Adenylyl cyclase to make cAMP
Ribosomes
Lysosomes

mcqs.q: Which gland is referred to as the master gland?
options: Pancreas
Pituitary
Thyroid
Adrenal
One daughter molecule contains both original strands; the other contains both new strands.
DNA replication produces two identical fully new molecules with no original material.
Action potentials get bigger as they travel along the axon.
Each new DNA molecule contains one original (parental) strand and one newly synthesised strand.

mcqs.q: What does the 'all-or-nothing' principle mean for action potentials?
options: Stronger stimuli produce larger action potentials.
Action potentials get bigger as they travel along the axon.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Once threshold is reached, the action potential fires at full size — sub-threshold stimuli produce no action potential.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Action potentials get bigger as they travel along the axon.
